next_exact_action.primary: Materialize [D]=1/2 div(F(w)/F(z)) in Pic^0(N)[2] from source-locked V6/modular divisor data, or equivalently compute the difference unramified Z/2 character on a basis of H1(N,F2).
next_exact_action.success_nonzero: If [D]!=0 is forced, O210 is excluded at this common-cover layer, subject to hostile audit.
next_exact_action.success_zero: If [D]=0, the common Beauville double-cover condition survives and work continues to the degree-81/full-V4 compatibility.

pic2_obstruction.definition: Write div(q)=2D. Then deg(D)=0 and [D] is a 2-torsion class in Pic^0(N).
pic2_obstruction.nonzero_meaning: A nonzero [D] is the unramified quadratic twist separating the two pullback double covers despite identical branch parity.

quadratic_pullback_lemma.proof: For characteristic not two, K(sqrt(a))=K(sqrt(b)) for nontrivial quadratic extensions iff a/b is a square.
quadratic_pullback_lemma.same_double_cover_iff: F(w)/F(z) is a square in K(N)^*
quadratic_pullback_lemma.setup: Choose a rational coordinate u on X(4)=P1 and F(u) with odd zero divisor at the six branch cusps of C0->X(4) and even pole divisor, so K(C0)=K(P1)(sqrt(F(u))). Let z,w in K(N) be the two modular factor maps of degrees 105 and 81.

valuation_parity_reduction.conclusion: Every valuation of q=F(w)/F(z) is even.
valuation_parity_reduction.exceptional_contacts: At every exceptional contact the retained adapter has A_z and A_w of the same parity, equal to parity(m). Thus m=1 contacts give odd valuation for both pullbacks and m=2 contacts give even valuation for both.
valuation_parity_reduction.odd_support: The common odd support is exactly the 210 m=1 exceptional contacts at O=210.
valuation_parity_reduction.poles: F can be chosen with even pole divisor (degree-six branch polynomial model), so pullback pole valuations are even.
valuation_parity_reduction.strict_boundary: A strict-boundary contribution to an X(4) cusp fiber has local degree 2*l, hence even valuation.
